items.title: Developing and implementing a remote patient management program at a large academic children's hospital.
items.abstract: Remote patient monitoring (RPM) can improve access, engagement, and clinical outcomes, yet evidence describing how health systems develop, scale, and sustain enterprise-wide RPM programs remains limited, particularly in pediatrics. We describe the development of a centralized RPM program at a large academic children's hospital and lessons learned from implementing 16 programs across diverse clinical settings. Beginning with a single cardiology pilot in 2021, we iteratively developed an enterprise RPM model spanning complex transitions from hospital to home, perioperative care, and specialty care. A centralized Digital Health team provided program intake and prioritization, implementation support, technology and electronic health record (EHR) integration, analytics, and ongoing optimization, while clinical divisions retained responsibility for clinical workflows and patient management. The portfolio expanded to 16 RPM programs. Experience across implementations demonstrated the importance of clearly defining the clinical or operational problem and measures of success before launch, identifying strong clinical champions, integrating RPM into existing workflows, selecting technology aligned with organizational and patient needs, and establishing sustainable operational and financial models. Centralized infrastructure enabled shared expertise, standardized measurement, and ongoing optimization while preserving specialty-specific clinical ownership. A centralized operational model with decentralized clinical ownership can support scalable pediatric RPM across diverse populations and workflows. Our experience demonstrates that successful enterprise RPM requires more than technology deployment; sustained growth depends on standardized implementation processes, clinical engagement, governance, measurement, equity considerations, and early planning for long-term sustainability.

items.title: Association of Enteral Chloral Hydrate with Benzodiazepine Exposure and Delirium After Pediatric Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Before-and-After Cohort Study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the association between the addition of enteral chloral hydrate to a postoperative sedation protocol and benzodiazepine exposure, sedation quality, withdrawal, delirium, and short-term clinical outcomes in children undergoing congenital heart surgery. Single-center retrospective before-and-after cohort study. Pediatric cardiac intensive care unit of a tertiary referral center. Eighty-six children who underwent congenital heart surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass, required postoperative mechanical ventilation for more than 24 hours, and received sedation for at least 24 hours. Patients were treated according to the institutional postoperative sedation protocol before (July 2021-June 2023) and after (August 2023-July 2025) implementation of enteral chloral hydrate as an adjunctive sedative. The primary endpoint was cumulative midazolam exposure during the pediatric cardiac intensive care unit stay. Secondary endpoints included sedative and analgesic requirements, sedation and pain scores, withdrawal, delirium, and clinical outcomes. Compared with the preprotocol group, the chloral hydrate group had significantly lower cumulative midazolam exposure (10.2 v 13.2 mg/kg, p = 0.010) and peak midazolam infusion rates (0.15 v 0.20 mg/kg/h, p < 0.001), and a lower observed frequency of delirium (14.6% v 37.8%, p = 0.015). No significant between-group differences were observed in sedation quality, pain scores, withdrawal, duration of mechanical ventilation, length of stay in the pediatric cardiac intensive care unit or hospital, or mortality. Addition of enteral chloral hydrate to a postoperative sedation protocol was associated with reduced benzodiazepine exposure and a lower observed frequency of delirium without statistically significant differences in sedation quality or short-term clinical outcomes. Prospective multicenter studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

Cardiovascular risk among individuals with and without a genetic mutation for familial hypercholesterolemia: A long-term study.
items.abstract: Patients with familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) are exposed to elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels from early life. Whether FH independently increases risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) remains uncertain. To compare the risk of developing ASCVD between individuals with and without FH mutations across different levels of LDL-C. A registry-based cohort study including patients genetically tested for FH from 1991 to 2023. Exposure was genetic mutation in the LDL, APOB, or PCSK-9 genes within the different LDL groups: LDL-C 7 mmol/L. ASCVD was defined as composite major adverse cardiac events (MACE) comprising myocardial infarction, cardiovascular death, angina pectoris, and stroke. An adjusted Cox proportional hazards model was used. The study included 2327 patients, comprising 958 with FH mutation and 1369 without. Mean follow-up time was 13.9 ± 9.8 years. LDL-C was significantly associated with the risk of future ASCVD, with a multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio (HR) of 1.17 (95%CI: 1.13-1.22, P  7 mmol/L HR 1.13 [95%CI: 0.91;1.41]) using patients without FH as reference. Genetic FH mutation did not confer additional risk when compared to individuals without an FH mutation but with similar LDL-C levels. These findings suggest that LDL-C levels - rather than FH mutation status - should guide the intensity of lipid-lowering therapy.

items.title: Self-reinforcing immunometabolic microneedles enable circuit-level lactate reprogramming to enhance solid tumor immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Excessive lactate accumulation in solid tumors disrupts metabolic-immune coordination within the tumor microenvironment, driving acidosis, immune suppression, and resistance to immunotherapy. Current lactate-targeting strategies mainly act on isolated metabolic nodes and therefore fail to restore coordinated control over lactate production, intracellular utilization, and extracellular immunosuppression. Here, we develop a self-reinforcing immunometabolic microneedle platform (LZH/PC MNs) to reconstruct the tumor lactate regulatory circuit at multiple levels. Calcium carbonate-mineralized photosynthetic cyanobacteria and lactate oxidase-loaded zeolitic imidazolate framework nanoparticles (LZH NPs) are hierarchically integrated into dissolvable microneedles for localized intratumoral delivery. In the acidic tumor microenvironment, calcium carbonate consumes protons to alleviate extracellular acidosis while replenishing calcium ions. Following cellular internalization, LZH NPs catalyze intracellular lactate oxidation to generate oxidative stress, thereby sustaining calcium overload and inducing immunogenic cell death. Meanwhile, light-driven photosynthetic oxygenation enhances lactate oxidase activity, destabilizes hypoxia-inducible factor 1α, suppresses glycolysis-driven lactate production, and promotes macrophage repolarization. Through the integrated regulation of extracellular acidosis alleviation, intracellular lactate depletion, and upstream metabolic inhibition, LZH/PC MNs restore lactate homeostasis, rewire tumor metabolic-immune crosstalk, and elicit systemic antitumor immunity against both primary and distant tumors. This work establishes tumor lactate metabolism as a circuit-level immunometabolic target and provides a generalizable strategy for overcoming lactate-driven immune resistance in solid tumors.

items.title: Beyond Hemostasis: Platelets as Drivers of Immune Suppression in Cancer.
items.abstract: Despite their primary role in hemostasis, pre-clinical evidence suggests that platelets also promote cancer progression. Mechanistically, platelets deliver tumor-supportive signals through direct contact or secreted mediators that can promote several cancer hallmarks, including angiogenesis, metastasis, and more recently, immune suppression. As the roles of platelets in cancer become ever more established in pre-clinical studies, the rationale for testing antiplatelet drugs in patients has also grown and now needs to be considered in the wider context of cancer immunotherapy. This review highlights recent mechanistic discoveries demonstrating how platelets promote tumor immune evasion and discusses how targeting platelets may synergize with cancer therapy.

Efficacy and safety of Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) or Entecavir (ETV) combined with interferon for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Whether tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) or entecavir (ETV) combined with pegylated interferon offers superior functional cure potential in chronic hepatitis B remains unclear. To compare the efficacy and safety of TDF plus interferon versus ETV plus interferon against their respective monotherapies. Systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 randomized controlled trials from six databases (inception to January 2026). TDF (300 mg/day) or ETV (0.5 mg/day) plus pegylated interferon alfa-2a/2b (180 µg/week) versus monotherapy. HBsAg reduction and HBeAg seroconversion. Risk of bias: Cochrane RoB 2; Certainty: GRADE. CRD42025632412. 2,575 patients were included. TDF plus interferon achieved markedly superior HBsAg reduction versus TDF monotherapy (OR 5.16, 95% CI 2.71-9.84; ARD 4.9%, 95% CI 2.0-9.9; NNT 20, 95% CI 10-50), whereas ETV plus interferon showed no significant benefit (OR 1.16, 95% CI 0.56-2.40; P = 0.006 for interaction). HBeAg seroconversion similarly favored TDF-based regimens (OR 2.25 vs. 1.63). HBV DNA negativity improved overall, although this effect was confined to TDF-based regimens. Safety data were highly heterogeneous (I² > 80% within both regimen subgroups) and derived from variable reporting standards; no reliable pooled estimate was constructed. Descriptive synthesis revealed no consistent excess toxicity for TDF-based or ETV-based combinations, though certainty remains very low. Sensitivity analyses excluding high-risk trials demonstrated robustness. GRADE certainty: moderate for serological outcomes, low for HBV DNA, very low for safety. TDF-based combination regimens were associated with superior functional cure potential compared with ETV-based alternatives, suggesting a potential efficacy hierarchy that prior pooled analyses obscured. TDF may represent a potential backbone option for patients seeking HBsAg loss, with ETV combinations remaining an appropriate alternative, particularly for those with TDF contraindications or baseline renal impairment or osteopenia. However, these findings are descriptive rather than prescriptive, derive specifically from predominantly HBeAg-positive Asian populations, and should not be generalized to other demographic or disease-stage groups without further validation. The moderate-to-low certainty of evidence, substantial methodological limitations, lack of blinded trials, and insufficient safety data to exclude differential renal or bone toxicity between backbones preclude definitive treatment recommendations. Confirmation in double-blind trials is needed.

items.title: lncRNA ZNF667-AS1 suppresses hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma by regulating miR-210-3p to upregulate CPEB2.
items.abstract: To explore the biological functions, clinical significance, and regulatory mechanism of long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) ZNF667-AS1 in hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). One hundred and seven patients with HBV-related HCC, one hundred and five patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and one hundred and five healthy controls were enrolled in this study. Real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) was used to detect the expression levels of ZNF667-AS1, miR-210-3p, CPEB2. The association between ZNF667-AS1 expression and clinical characteristics of patients were analyzed, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate its diagnostic value. Bioinformatics prediction and dual-luciferase reporter assays were conducted to verify the targeted associations between ZNF667-AS1 and miR-210-3p, as well as between miR-210-3p and CPEB2. Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) and Transwell assays were applied to assess the biological functions of HCC cells after cell transfection. The expression levels of ZNF667-AS1 and CPEB2 were significantly downregulated in tissue samples from patients with HBV-related HCC and in HBV-associated HCC cell lines. ROC curve analysis showed the area under the curve (AUC) of ZNF667-AS1 for diagnosing HBV-related HCC from CHB reached 0.841. miR-210-3p was validated as a direct target of ZNF667-AS1, and a significant negative correlation was observed between their expression levels. Overexpression of ZNF667-AS1 inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of HCC cells, whereas this inhibitory effect was reversed by transfection with miR-210-3p mimic. LncRNA ZNF667-AS1 is downregulated in HBV-related HCC and exerts in vitro tumor‑suppressive effects by targeting miR-210-3p to upregulate CPEB2 expression, thus providing a potential auxiliary biomarker for HBV-related HCC diagnosis and a novel regulatory axis for understanding disease pathogenesis.

items.title: Diagnostic performance of liver biochemical and hemostatic markers for assessing cirrhosis severity in chronic hepatitis B.
items.abstract: This study aimed to explore the utility of liver biochemical and hemostatic (including coagulation, anticoagulation, and fibrinolysis) markers for assessing cirrhosis severity in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients. In this current study, a total of 28 healthy controls and 78 patients with CHB-related cirrhosis were enrolled. Routine laboratory markers including platelet count (PLT), albumin (ALB), total bilirubin (TBIL), creatinine (CREA), prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), factor VIII (FVIII), prothrombin activity (PA), protein S (PS), protein C (PC), antithrombin III (AT-III) and D-dimer (D-D) were measured. Correlations between the measured parameters and Child-Pugh score (CPS)/ Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score (MELD) were also explored. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the ability of these indicators to discriminate between mild and moderate-to-severe CHB-related cirrhosis. Patients with CHB-related cirrhosis exhibited significantly lower levels of ALB, PA, PS, PC, AT-III, and PLT, and significantly higher levels of TBIL, PT, APTT, FVIII, and D-D, compared with healthy controls (p < 0.05). ALB, PA, AT-III, PS, and PC showed significant negative correlations with both CPS and MELD (p < 0.01). TBIL, PT, and APTT demonstrated significant positive correlations (p < 0.01). ROC curve analysis revealed that AT-III achieved an AUC of 0.95 (95% CI: 0.88-1.00) for distinguishing cirrhosis severity, followed by PC (AUC: 0.87) and PA (AUC: 0.87). As expected, Child-Pugh components (ALB, TBIL, PT) showed strong associations with the score. Among markers not incorporated into the CPS, AT-III is significantly associated with the severity of CHB-related cirrhosis and exhibits promising discriminatory ability for staging CHB-related cirrhosis. It may support a low-cost, objective framework for dynamic monitoring of HBV-related cirrhosis progression. Although ALB, TBIL, and PT were also correlated with disease severity, these associations are subject to incorporation bias and thus represent confirmatory rather than novel findings.

items.title: A hospital-based micro-elimination strategy for hepatitis C in western China: a retrospective before-after study.
items.abstract: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains a major public health burden in China, with low rates of diagnosis and treatment. Hospital-based "micro-elimination" strategies have been proposed to identify and link high-risk patients to care, but evidence from real-world implementations, particularly in western China, is limited. This study aimed to evaluate changes in HCV screening, diagnosis, and follow-up rates following the implementation of a hospital-based micro-elimination strategy at a tertiary hospital in western China. This retrospective, uncontrolled before-after study was conducted at a single tertiary hospital in Xi'an, China. The study comprised a pre-intervention phase (October 2017-September 2020) and a post-intervention phase (October 2020-May 2022). Hospital inpatient and laboratory databases were used to identify patients with positive anti-HCV or HCV-RNA tests. The micro-elimination strategy included: (i) identification of three high-risk groups using retrospective and routine data retrieval; (ii) telephone follow-up and patient education; and (iii) educational lectures for non-specialist healthcare workers. Primary outcomes were changes in anti-HCV screening rates, HCV diagnostic confirmation rates (HCV-RNA testing among anti-HCV positive), and loss to follow-up rates. Secondary outcomes included healthcare worker knowledge scores. Comparisons between phases were made using chi-square tests and t-tests, with no adjustment for confounders. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. After the MES conducted, the rate of HCV screening and diagnosis were significantly improved, while the lost follow-up rate were markedly decreased compared with the previous three years (all P < 0.001). The results showed that patients, who were males, aged above 40, attended to gastroenterology, respiratory and critical care medicine, and neurology departments, has higher rate of HCV infection. Notably, disease education tours significantly improved the non-specialist healthcare workers' knowledge about HCV infection, policy awareness and preventive methods (all P < 0.001). In addition, 86.8% of high-risk patients demonstrated a strong willingness to accept further testing and start DAAs treatment after receiving follow-up and health education. The implementation of this hospital-based micro-elimination strategy was associated with an observed increase in HCV screening and diagnosis rates and a decrease in loss to follow-up compared with the pre-intervention period. Although causality cannot be established due to the uncontrolled before-after design, these findings suggest that such a strategy is feasible, low-cost, and may be a valuable component of hospital-based HCV elimination efforts. Further controlled studies are needed to confirm its effectiveness.

Three-dimensional multimodal fractal dynamics integrating spatial metabolism, cytoarchitecture, and perfusion for preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion in colorectal liver metastases.
items.abstract: Accurately predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) preoperatively remains a core challenge for precision surgical decision-making in patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM). This study developed and validated a three-dimensional multimodal fractal dynamic model (FRAC-3D) that integrates spatial metabolism, cytoarchitecture, and blood perfusion, aiming to non-invasively identify MVI status preoperatively and evaluate patient prognosis. Utilizing a retrospective nested cohort design, stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (sIPTW) was applied to the derivation cohort (n = 100) for baseline debiasing. A core cohort of 145 patients with complete PET/CT, CE-MRI, and DWI imaging was ultimately included. Spatial metabolic fractal dimension (FD_PET), architectural fractal dimension (FD_ADC), and perfusion fractal acceleration (Afd_MRI) were extracted to construct the FRAC-3D model. The model's discrimination, calibration, and clinical benefit were validated in an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 45). Multivariable analysis confirmed that FD_ADC is the strongest independent predictor of MVI (OR = 3.85, 95% CI: 2.45-6.04, P < 0.001). The FRAC-3D model achieved an AUC of 0.938 and a negative predictive value of 96.2% in the validation cohort. Compared with the dual-modal model, FRAC-3D significantly improved risk restratification (continuous NRI = 0.425, P < 0.001). A "highly chaotic" imaging phenotype, identified based on fractal feature clustering, demonstrated an MVI incidence as high as 96.7% and a median recurrence-free survival (RFS) of only 5.2 months. Through the cross-validation of multidimensional biophysical features, the FRAC-3D model enables high-precision preoperative prediction of MVI status. This study advances the perioperative assessment of CRLM from traditional 'static anatomical metrics' into a novel dimension of 'microenvironmental dynamic evolution', providing a robust, physics-driven tool for individualized surgical margin planning and the precise stratification of targeted neoadjuvant therapy.

items.title: PSA testing and receipt of curative treatment in elderly Japanese men with prostate cancer: a population-based study.
items.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate whether regular prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing is associated with the receipt of curative treatment for prostate cancer among men in Japan and to identify associated factors. A retrospective analysis was conducted using the claims data from the National Health Insurance and Late-Stage Elderly Health Care System in Saga Prefecture between March 2014 and March 2022. Patients were categorized into PSA testing (≥ 1 test ≥ 6 months before treatment) and non-PSA testing groups. Curative treatment was defined as either a radical prostatectomy or carbon-ion radiotherapy. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify the factors associated with curative treatment. Among 2,200 patients, 737 (33.5%) underwent PSA testing, and 708 (32.2%) received curative treatment. Patients who underwent PSA testing were older and more likely to participate in Specific Health Checkups. The proportion receiving curative treatment was higher in the PSA testing group (36.4% vs. 30.1%, p < 0.001). Age (OR = 0.85), PSA testing (OR = 1.53), and participation in Specific Health Checkups, which do not include PSA testing, were independently associated with curative treatment (OR = 1.64). PSA testing was associated with a higher likelihood of receiving curative treatment for prostate cancer. Participation in Specific Health Checkups may reflect a population more engaged in preventive healthcare or with greater access to screening opportunities.

items.title: Diagnostic performance of GAAD, PIVKA-II and AFP in hepatocellular carcinoma, chronic liver disease and healthy population: evidence from a Malaysian cohort.
items.abstract: The aim of the current study was to evaluate the diagnostic performances of GAAD score, PIVKA-II and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) surveillance in HCC, chronic liver disease (CLD) and healthy controls (HC) subjects from the northeastern Peninsular Malaysia. This was a single-center cross-sectional study. The GAAD value was calculated using the Elecsys® GAAD calculator. Serum PIVKA-II and AFP levels were measured using the Elecsys® electrochemiluminescence immunoassay method. Diagnostic performance of these tests were evaluated based on area under the curve (AUC), optimal cutoff levels, sensitivity (Se), specificity (Sp), positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV). Of the 128 enrolled subjects,99 were included (33 HCC, 33 CLD, and 33 HC). GAAD score, PIVKA-II, and AFP levels were significantly higher in patients with HCC than in those with CLD and HC (all p < 0.05). For differentiating HCC from CLD, GAAD at a cutoff of 2.57 demonstrated the highest Se (81.8%) and Sp (72.7%), with an AUC of 0.873 (95% CI 0.791-0.955). PIVKA-II at a cut-off of 28.4 ng/mL showed Se and Sp of 75.8% and 69.7%, respectively, with an AUC of 0.842 (95% CI 0.748-0.936). AFP at a cutoff of 20 ng/mL demonstrated lower Se (51.5%) but higher Sp (90.9%), with an AUC of 0.834 (95% CI 0.730-0.938). For differentiating HCC from HC, GAAD and PIVKA-II achieved 100% Sp and PPV, whereas AFP maintained 100% Sp but lower Se (51.52%). Overall, GAAD exhibited the best balance of sensitivity and specificity for HCC detection, while PIVKA-II provided complementary diagnostic value due to its high specificity. The GAAD score demonstrated superior diagnostic performance compared with both PIVKA-II and AFP in differentiating HCC from CLD and HC subjects, supporting its potential utility in HCC surveillance. In addition, PIVKA-II showed better diagnostic performance than AFP.

items.title: FATP5 loss in hepatocellular carcinoma cells orchestrates tumor-promoting microenvironment by inducing passive long-chain fatty acid accumulation within tumor-associated endothelial cells.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by severe immunosuppression and metabolic reprogramming, yet the spatial dynamics of lipid flux between malignant and stromal cells remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a profound, type-specific metabolic rewiring in HCC driven by the widespread downregulation of fatty acid transport protein 5 (FATP5). FATP5 deficiency in malignant cells selectively attenuates the uptake of long-chain fatty acids (LCFAs), creating an extracellular lipid surplus that is passively sequestered by neighboring FATP3-expressing tumor-associated endothelial cells (TECs). Within TECs, accumulated LCFAs function as endogenous ligands that activate the nuclear receptor PPARγ, culminating in the robust transcriptional upregulation and paracrine secretion of the chemokine CXCL12. Endothelial-derived CXCL12 subsequently engages CXCR4 on infiltrating CD8 + T cells, inducing PD-1 expression and driving terminal T-cell exhaustion, thereby establishing an immunosuppressive niche that accelerates tumor progression. Importantly, our data suggest that HCC subtypes marked by FATP5 depletion and CXCL12 + TEC enrichment may possess potential therapeutic susceptibility to PPARγ antagonism or anti-PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade. Besides affecting the secretory function of TECs, accumulated LCFAs can impair endothelial barrier function, thereby creating a microenvironment with hematogenous metastasis risk. Collectively, our findings delineate a novel tumor-promoting microenvironment cascade orchestrated by LCFA spatial redistribution, providing a promising mechanistic foundation to support the future development of targeted precision interventions for FATP5-low HCC. Liver cancer is a deadly disease known for shutting down the body’s immune defense and altering how tumor cells use nutrients like fatty acids. In this study, we investigated how fat molecules move between cancer cells and neighboring healthy cells, and how this affects the body’s ability to fight the tumor. We discovered that when cancer cells lose a specific protein called FATP5, they stop absorbing long-chain fatty acids. This leaves excess long-chain fatty acids in the tumor’s surroundings, which are then soaked up by nearby blood vessel cells. This fat overload triggers these blood vessel cells to release a chemical signal that exhausts and disables nearby immune cells, allowing the cancer to grow and spread. Crucially, our findings reveal that therapies targeting this fat-driven process, combined with existing immune-boosting drugs, could offer a powerful, personalized treatment for patients with this specific type of liver cancer.
